entries.reason: One carrier, ENG-003-A-CZ-A7 ('If we painted…, people ___'), three carrying options. The added sentence 'Use 'would have' only when the if part has 'had'.' rules out 'would have known' here, which is an improvement. But (1) as an English-grammar claim 'only' is false: mixed conditionals put 'would have' after an if part with no 'had' ('If she were more careful, she would have noticed'; 'If I were you, I would have told him'). A necessary-condition rule stated as absolute is the kind of claim this pass exists to stop. (2) 'would be knowing' (1 of 3 carrying options, the description's 'impossible modal form' half) is still served by no wording: the child used 'would' and the hint tells them 'would' is right. So the result helps 2 of 3 options and contains one over-strong grammar claim. Suggested direction: soften to ''Would have' goes with an if part that has 'had'.' and add a sentence for the impossible form, e.g. that 'know' does not take -ing after 'would be'; then re-screen.

resultText.childHint: An imagined if takes 'would'. A real if takes 'will'. Use 'would have' only when the if part has 'had'.
